title: Neurobiology, B.S. (Eberly College of Science)
notes: University Park. The bulletin's own suggested plan interleaves two separate requirements confusingly ('BIOL 222 or BIOL 161 & 162' appearing in both Second Year terms) — resolved against the cleaner Requirements-for-the-Major list: BIOL 161/162 (Anatomy) are separate prescribed courses from the BIOL 222-or-322 (Genetics) pick. BIOL 322 was chosen over BIOL 222 for the genetics requirement since its prerequisite (BIOL 230W) is already part of this plan's own core intro sequence, while BIOL 222's prerequisite (BIOL 110/141) is not otherwise needed here. 'etm' marks the gateway courses (BIOL 110, BIOL 230W) everything downstream depends on. Post-parens-fix re-scrape revealed CHEM 110's real prereq is MATH 22 (a placement threshold below Calc I that a MATH-140-track student has already tested past, but the bulletin's prereq text never says so explicitly), and MATH 22 has its own real chain (MATH 22 needs MATH 21, which needs MATH 4, which needs MATH 3) -- none of MATH 3/4/21/22 were in the plan, permanently blocking CHEM 110 and its downstream cascade (CHEM 111/112/113/210/212/213; BMB 211 needs CHEM 210/202; STAT 250 needs MATH 21 directly). Added MATH 3 (Semester 1), MATH 4 (Semester 2), MATH 21 (Semester 3), and MATH 22 (Semester 4) explicitly to complete the real chain, matching the fix used for MATSCI/ME/METEO/MICRB/MINE's identical CHEM 110 gap. 2026-08-27 verification against the live bulletin's fully-enumerated Group A/B/C/D lists found two real gaps beyond the electives being previously unwired: (1) the bulletin requires 6 credits from Group A specifically ('at least 6 credits from Group A ... 3 credits from Group B ... 3 credits from Group C ... and 3 credits from Group D'), but only one 3-credit Group A slot existed -- added a second. (2) 'Supporting Courses and Related Areas: Select 19-20 credits from department list' was modeled as only 3 generic 'Elective' slots (9 credits) -- renamed to 'Supporting Course (department list)' and added 4 more slots to reach 19 credits total. All 5 Group slots are now wired via 'match' on the bulletin's own real course lists (see each item's own notes); the 7 Supporting Course slots are wired via open_elective (min_level 200, excluding BIOL 496/SC 295/395/495 independent-study/co-op) since the bulletin names no further specific list beyond 'department list'. These additions (13 more credits) pushed the plan's own total past what fit at the original 17cr/semester cap, so max_credits_per_semester was raised to 18, the same precedent used across dozens of other majors' plans whenever a correction adds real credits (see PHYS-2026.json's notes for the fuller rationale).
